watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major update for Apple Watch, introducing a practical new feature to extend Apple Watch battery life: "Active Battery Extension Notification."

watchOS 27 can proactively extend Apple Watch battery life by disabling unused features

watchOS 27 is on the way, bringing two new apps, a useful new tap gesture, a default new home screen layout, three health-related upgrades, and more to Apple Watch.

Another new addition in watchOS 27 aims to extend your Apple Watch battery life.

"Active Battery Extension Notification" is a brand-new type of alert that may appear on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery extension notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected certain features you've never used, and disabling them will help conserve battery life.

These features include Gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function for invoking Siri, and "Start Workout" reminders.

Each of these features involves background processing, which places a certain drain on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you have never used these features, it will automatically disable them and send a "Battery Extension Notification" to inform you of the change, giving you the option to keep them enabled.

If you do use these features regularly, you won't receive this notification. Of course, you can also go to Settings at any time to disable them yourself in exchange for longer battery life.

Apple did not specify how much extra battery life disabling these features will actually provide, but it's clear the power savings are worth them building this brand-new battery extension feature.

Do you normally use features like "Raise to Speak," Gestures, or "Start Workout" reminders on your Apple Watch? Will you choose to keep them enabled in the future? Let us know in the comments.
